excerpt: SDG 7 is often talked about as a global target for other places. Looking closer, its promise of affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy is surprisingly local.
body:
Sustainable Development Goal 7 aims to *"ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all."* When I first read it, I filed it mentally under international development—something about electrification in other parts of the world. This week's readings made me realise how local it is.

As part of my coursework, my team compared SDG 7 (Affordable & Clean Energy) progress across Norway, Brazil, and Namibia - countries with dramatically different Human Development Index rankings (2, 84, and 136).

Here’s what surprised us:

* Norway ranks #2 globally on HDI and runs almost entirely on clean hydropower, yet its economy still leans heavily on petroleum exports. High human development doesn't automatically mean a sustainable energy system.
* Brazil is nearly 100% electrified with a huge renewable mix, but affordability and regional inequality remain major barriers. Energy access does not equal energy affordability.
* Namibia has some of the world’s best solar potential, yet roughly half its population still lacks reliable electricity, largely because of costly rural grid infrastructure and cost-reflective tariffs.

The biggest driver of these differences wasn’t renewable potential, all three countries have plenty. It was GNI per capita and public policy choice. Economic capacity, more than education or life expectancy, determines whether a country can finance the infrastructure needed to turn energy potential into energy access.



## Key takeaways

> * SDG 7 is about everyone, everywhere — including communities in wealthy countries.
> * Closing theSDG 7 gap isn’t just a technology problem - it’s a financing, governance, andpublic-policy problem.
> * Local ownership and efficiency are two of the most direct ways to make progress.



Grateful to Dr. Elaina Guilmette for pushing our cohort to dig past the headline numbers and interrogate the “why” behind the data. 🙏

💬What’s one policy you think could accelerate clean energy access in resource-rich but infrastructure-poor regions? I’d love to hear your take below.

title: SDG 7: 🌍⚡ Three countries, three very different energy stories - and a lesson in what “development” really means.
